name: Sahrawi nationalism
summary: Sahrawi nationalism demands that the people of the former Spanish Sahara exercise self-determination and found an independent state, the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic, over the whole colonial territory. It treats Moroccan control as occupation, claims the territory's resources for the Sahrawi people, and was organised through the Polisario Front's armed struggle since 1973. Scholarship describes it as postcolonial rather than ethnic, tied to the colonial borders.
scope: The nationalism of the Polisario Front and the SADR for independence over Western Sahara within its colonial borders, as stated in the 2015 SADR constitution and the 2025 expanded Polisario proposal (S/2025/664) and as defined by Barreñada (who describes Sahrawi nationalism as postcolonial, not ethnic) and the encyclopedia entry on the Polisario. It excludes the ethnic-Sahrawi territory outside the colony, Algerian policy, and any socialist programme not stated in those texts. Positions the 2015 text defers until independence (parties, market economy) count only as stated.

national-self-determination.rationale: The 2015 constitution (Art. 24) commits the state to defend the Sahrawi people's right to independence, and the 2025 proposal (paras 10-13) calls the right inalienable, non-negotiable and not lapsed by time.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The preamble speaks of liberating the homeland 'from colonialism and subsequently from occupation', and the proposal (paras 4, 13) holds that the 1975 Madrid Agreement transferred no sovereignty and that a fait accompli since 1975 cannot overtake the right to self-determination.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Art. 1 defines the state as Saguia el Hamra and Rio de Oro 'within its internationally recognised borders'; Barreñada records that the movement has always accepted the intangibility of the colonial borders and tied the nation to the colonial territory, not the ethnic one.

national-resource-control.rationale: Art. 17 makes mineral, energy and other resources public property of the people, and proposal para 41 holds that economic activity in the territory without the Sahrawi people's consent is unlawful.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Art. 13 says the State derives its legitimacy from the will of the people, and proposal para 12 makes the freely expressed will of the Sahrawi people the basis of any solution.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The movement's central procedural demand is a UN and African Union supervised referendum in which the Sahrawi people choose the territory's status, with independence among the options (proposal paras 11, 16, 19).

political-violence-never.rationale: The preamble founds the state on the war of liberation declared in 1973 and Art. 22 gives the army the task of attaining independence; the movement does not hold political violence to be never justified.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: The preamble celebrates the 1973 war of liberation against colonialism and then occupation, and Art. 48 makes defending the country and taking part in its liberation a sacred obligation of every citizen.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Art. 11 directs the people's institutions to preserve the values of the people and defend their identity and national personality.

conscription.rationale: Art. 49 makes national service an obligation on all citizens who meet the legal conditions.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Art. 22 makes the Sahrawi People's Liberation Army the armed forces of the State and guarantor of national sovereignty.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Arts 25-26 guarantee all citizens the same rights without discrimination as to ethnicity, race, gender, religion or opinion and equality before the law.

women-suffrage.rationale: Art. 33 makes every citizen meeting legal conditions eligible to vote and be voted for, and Art. 25 bars discrimination by gender.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale is about national or state-level self-government or equality in general, not Indigenous self-government, and the statement now asks whether new Indigenous self-government arrangements should guarantee women's equal participation.

reviewHistory.rationale: Art. 42 commits the State to ensure women's political, economic, social and cultural participation in building the country; it is a state provision, not a rule for self-government arrangements of national groups as such.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The preamble holds that liberty and dignity need a society 'where law is sovereign', and the oath of Art. 56 binds the President to abide by the constitution.

separated-powers.rationale: Proposal para 32 states that the Sahrawi State will embrace a separation of powers, and the constitution gives the judiciary independence (Art. 117) and a legislature that can censure the government (Arts 103-107).

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Arts 69 and 76 require the National Council to approve the government's programme and annual operating budget.

head-of-state-dissolves-parliament.rationale: Art. 107 lets the President answer a censure motion by dissolving the National Council, with early elections within 40 days (Art. 108).

head-commands-forces.rationale: Art. 57 makes the President Commander-in-Chief and Art. 53 has the President appoint and dismiss the Prime Minister and ministers.

elective-rulers.rationale: The President is elected (Art. 51, by the Polisario congress by secret ballot) and Art. 19 bars nepotism in office; no hereditary office is provided for.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The head of state is elected by a congress (Art. 51) and Art. 19 criminalises serving nepotism through office, which excludes succession by a child.

separate-church-state.rationale: Art. 2 makes Islam the State religion and a main source of law, which is not strict separation; the constitution also draws on the Universal Declaration and modern demands.

traditional-family.rationale: Art. 7 calls the family the foundation of society, based on religious, ethical and national values and historical heritage.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Art. 37 gives all citizens a right to protection and healthcare and has the State ensure protection against diseases and epidemics.

legal-duty-to-work.rationale: Art. 38 declares that having employment is a right, an obligation and an honour for all citizens.

social-market-economy.rationale: The constitution pairs social rights to education, health and housing (Arts 36-40) with a market economy and private initiative after independence (Art. 46); the proposal (para 32) also adopts a market-based economy.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The preamble stresses the need to build the Grand Maghreb and concretise African and Arab unity, and the proposal (paras 33-34) commits the state to Arab Maghreb Union integration and the African Union's Agenda 2063.

civilizational-union.rationale: The preamble calls for building the Grand Maghreb and concretising African Unity and Arab Unity, and Art. 24 backs Maghreb unity.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: The proposal (paras 48-50) guarantees Moroccan citizens' rights and property, offers nationality to those established there, and limits departure to voluntary return.

population-transfer.rationale: The proposal (paras 48-50) says no one will be persecuted for opinions held in the referendum and that return to Morocco will be voluntary, so pressure on a minority to leave is excluded.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Barreñada states that Sahrawi nationalism is not ethnic but postcolonial, and builds the nation on the colonial territory, leaving part of the ethnic group outside the state.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Barreñada records that the movement's claim is tied to the colonial territory and the intangibility of colonial borders, so ethnic Sahrawis living outside it are left outside the state.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Barreñada records that the claim is to the former Spanish colony, not to lands where ethnic Sahrawis live in neighbouring states.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Barreñada describes the Sahrawi nation as a modern concept bound to the colonial territory although Hassaniya speakers live across several states.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Barreñada calls the Sahrawi national identity a recent product of late colonialism, while the constitution preamble speaks of a long resistance that has never stopped through the people's history.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Art. 15 prohibits abandoning or ceding any part of the national territory, and the proposal accepts only the referendum outcome as settling the status of the land.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The proposal (para 45) solemnly commits the Sahrawi State to respect other states' sovereignty and territorial integrity and not to let its territory be used for aggression.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Art. 44 guarantees legally resident aliens the right to practise their religions and customs.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Art. 45 guarantees the private property of legally resident aliens and the proposal (para 49) protects Moroccan residents' properties.

democracy-best.rationale: The constitution commits the state to democratic institutions and the proposal promises a multiparty system (para 32), but Mormul reports criticism that Polisario in practice functions as a party and the system as a one-party one.
